title: A herd agent can declare its workspace-trust store and bee pre-flights it
action: D5 brings workspace trust back into scope, and the reason is structural: `bee worktree new` mints a brand-new directory every time, so a first herding run into a fresh worktree meets an untrusted-workspace dialog every time. Proven live 2026-08-21 — three concurrent agy runs into a fresh worktree all sat at 'Do you trust this folder?'. The herd entry's auto-approve flag does not reach it: `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions` covers TOOL permissions only, and `agy --help` shows no trust flag and no trust subcommand. The store is a plain JSON file: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, key `trustedWorkspaces`, an array of absolute paths. Make it declarable, not hard-coded. (1) `wave.rs`: the named-agent registry already accepts either a bare argv array or `{argv, env}` — `parse_registry_entry` at wave.rs:226-241, entry struct at wave.rs:140-144, registry at wave.rs:250-261. Follow that exact house style and add one more OPTIONAL object field, a workspace-trust declaration naming the JSON file to read and the array key inside it that holds trusted absolute paths. Expand a leading `~` in the file path. Keep the array shape, built-in entries and the plain `agent_command` path working byte-identically, and keep the existing fail-open rule: a malformed declaration drops the entry rather than poisoning the registry, exactly as a bad env key already does (wave.rs:205-219). Carry it through `resolve_agent_command` (wave.rs:331-343) alongside the env map. (2) `run.rs`: in `execute_new`, after the command is resolved (around run.rs:1108-1118) and BEFORE the pane split and `agent_start`, run the pre-flight when the resolved entry declares one — read the file, and if the run's absolute `--cwd` is not already in the array, append it and write the file back atomically with the crate's existing atomic-write helper. This is FAIL-OPEN and must be loud: a missing file, unparsable JSON, a missing or non-array key, or an unwritable file all emit one warning line naming the file and what was wrong, then let the run proceed — hps-7's diagnosis pass will name the dialog if the agent then stalls on it. Never fail a run because a foreign tool's config could not be pre-seeded, and never rewrite anything in that file except appending one absolute path to the named array. (3) Document the new field where the registry entry is already specified: the `herding.agents` section of `skills/bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md`, and a live example in `.bee/config-sample.json` next to the existing agent entries — the sample must show `agy-flash` declaring the Antigravity store, since that is the case that motivated it. Tests: the object form parsing with and without the declaration; a malformed declaration dropping the entry; `~` expansion; the pre-flight appending an absent path; the pre-flight leaving an already-present path untouched (no rewrite); and each fail-open branch warning and proceeding.

truths: A herd agent entry can declare a workspace-trust JSON file and array key, and the bare-array form still works unchanged
The pre-flight runs before the pane split and appends the run's cwd only when absent
Every failure mode warns and lets the run proceed — a foreign tool's config never fails a bee run
The config sample shows agy-flash declaring the Antigravity trust store
